title: Ex Vivo Perfusion Culture of Large Blood Vessels in a 3D Printed Bioreactor
protocol: Fabricate the insert by 3D printing using the provided 3D model.
Use selective laser sintering or stereolithography as appropriate alternatives for manufacturing.
Consider polyamide 12 (PA12) as a material candidate due to its liquid retention and heat resistance properties.
Fabricate silicon gaskets and polycarbonate washers by laser cutting.
Sterilize all components following the instructions provided.
Assemble two fabricated inserts under laminar flow conditions.
Attach two connected three-way valves to the reservoir's R1 port.
Connect the resulting outlet to the peristaltic pump's head using a tube equipped with a one-way valve.
Connect the pump head to the reaction chamber's C4 port using system tubing equipped with a one-way valve.
Connect the reaction chamber port C1 to soft wall tubing, and this to the resistance channel.
Extend the resistance channel with system tubing, creating a return channel and closing the luminal circulation loop by connecting to the reservoir at R5.
Create an overflow channel by connecting the reaction chamber C3 to the reservoir R3 with system tubing.
Attach a ventilation filter through R2.
Connect a syringe containing air and media to the reaction chamber C6 to create a pressure dampener.
Prime the system with perfusion medium (DMEM + 10% FBS + 1% penicillin-streptomycin + 1% amphotericin B + 30% dextran) through the media exchange ports and the reservoir.
Collect the left and right common carotid arteries, minimizing direct handling of the arterial tissue.
Place the tissue in cold transport media.
Remove excess connective tissue from the tissue using a scalpel blade.
Trim the ends of the tissue using a scalpel blade.
Wash the tissue twice in cold transport media.
Place the tissue on an orbital shaker in transport media for at least 30 min.
Connect a non-branching segment of the artery to the bioreactor system using two barbed luer connectors.
Fix the connection in place using a vessel bond.
Gently flow media through the artery to verify patency.
Fill the reaction space with perfusion media.
Gently fill the luminal circulation loop with media to eliminate any remaining air from the system.
Connect the reaction space with the previously assembled perfusion system.
Place the perfusion system in a 37 °C incubator with 5% CO2.
Connect the perfusion system to a peristaltic pump.
Connect any additional acquisition systems, such as pressure sensors.
Leave the system to equilibrate overnight with a media flow rate of ~10-15 mL/min.
Increase the flow incrementally (+1 rpm every hour) until reaching 35 mL/min.
Monitor the system periodically for leaks.
Exchange 50% of the media every 3 days by connecting a syringe filled with fresh media to the media exchange port closer to the pump and an empty syringe to the port closer to the reservoir.
Harvest the tissue from the reaction chamber at the end of the experiment using sterile surgical scissors to trim the ends connected to the bioreactor.
Clean and sterilize the system for further use after dismantling it.
Fix the harvested sample in 4% paraformaldehyde overnight at 4 °C.
Embed the tissue in optimal cutting temperature (OCT).
Freeze the embedded tissue by immersion in iso-pentane cooled in liquid nitrogen.
Obtain cryo-sections of 3-5 mm thickness using a cryostat.
Block the slices for 1 h at room temperature with 20% [v/v] goat serum in PBS.
Incubate the slices overnight at 4 °C with primary rabbit antibody against CD31 diluted 1:50 in PBS.
Wash the slices three times with PBS for 5 min.

Incubate for 1 h at 37 °C with fluorescently labeled goat anti-rabbit secondary antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS and α-smooth muscle actin (SMA) directly conjugated fluorescent antibody diluted 1:200 in PBS.
Wash three times with PBS for 5 min.
Stain the nuclei with DAPI diluted 1:1,000 in PBS for 10 min at room temperature.
Incubate with 0.1% (w/v) Sudan Black in 70% (v/v) ethanol for 10 min at room temperature to reduce tissue autofluorescence.
Wash the tissue with abundant deionized water.
Mount the slides in the mounting medium.
Image the samples with a confocal laser scanning microscope.
